marks.gloss_en: אמרינן קל וחומר: קריאת שמע דאורייתא פוסק, הלל דרבנן מבעיא?! -- if one interrupts the Shema, which is Torah law, surely one interrupts Hallel, which is rabbinic
או דלמא פרסומי ניסא עדיף -- or perhaps publicising the miracle is weightier, so Hallel and the Megilla may not be interrupted
פוסק, ואין בכך כלום -- one interrupts, and there is nothing in it (R' Chiyya rules with the first horn; he gives no reason)
R' Chiyya: [in Hallel and the Megilla] one interrupts, and there is nothing in it
תניא נמי הכי -- the baraita gives R' Meir's 'needless to say he responds' and R' Yehuda's clauses, as the reconstruction has them

the baraita: one reading the Shema whom his teacher or a greater man meets -- R' Meir: at the breaks greets out of respect and needless to say responds, in the middle greets out of fear and needless to say responds; R' Yehuda: in the middle greets out of fear and responds out of respect, at the breaks greets out of respect and responds to anyone
איני?! והא רב בר שבא איקלע לגביה דרבינא ... ולא פסיק ליה -- Ravina did not interrupt Hallel for Rav bar Shaba on such a day
Rav bar Shaba came to Ravina on a day the individual does not complete Hallel, and he did not interrupt for him
שאני רב בר שבא דלא חשיב עליה דרבינא -- Rav bar Shaba is different: he was not important to Ravina
R' Yochanan: the halakha follows R' Yehuda, who said one may not interrupt between 'eloheichem' and 'emet veyatziv'
(וכדרב אידי בר אבין דאמר) -- as Rav Idi bar Avin said in Rav Yitzchak bar Ashyan's name: it is forbidden to attend to one's affairs before praying
Rav Yitzchak bar Ashyan: it is forbidden for a person to attend to his affairs before he prays
מתיב רב ששת: בפרקים שואל מפני הכבוד ומשיב -- the mishnah permits greeting at the breaks of the Shema, which is before prayer
the mishnah (13a.17): at the breaks [of the Shema] one greets out of respect, and responds
תרגמה רבי אבא: במשכים לפתחו -- the dictum concerns one who goes early to his fellow's door (= p_abba_mashkim_lefitcho)
R' Abba: [Rav's dictum speaks of] one who goes early to [his fellow's] door
Rav: whoever greets his fellow before he prays, it is as if he made him a bama
Shmuel: [bameh read as written --] in what did you esteem this one, and not God?
[as first given:] whoever attends to his affairs before he prays, it is as if he built a bama
Rav Yitzchak bar Ashyan: whoever prays and afterwards sets out on his way, the Holy One attends to his affairs for him
תניא נמי הכי: מטעמת אינה טעונה ברכה, והשרוי בתענית טועם ואין בכך כלום
R' Ami: he tastes, and there is nothing in it
may one who is fasting taste? [Either] he accepted on himself [abstention from] eating and drinking, and this is not that; or perhaps he accepted [abstention from] benefit, and this is that
R' Ami would taste [while fasting] up to the measure of a revi'it
R' Zeira: whoever goes seven nights without a dream is called 'evil'
R' Yochanan: whoever sates himself with words of Torah and goes to sleep, they do not bring him evil tidings
